description: The second book (Sabhā Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the assembly hall (sabhā) of Yudhiṣṭhira, the Rājasūya sacrifice, and the fateful game of dice.

title: Mahābhārata Śānti Parva
description: The twelfth book (Śānti Parva) of the Mahābhārata, the longest book, containing Bhīṣma's teachings on rājadharma, āpad-dharma, and mokṣa from his bed of arrows.

title: Mahābhārata Sauptika Parva
description: The tenth book (Sauptika Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the night raid (sauptika) by Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman on the sleeping Pāṇḍava army.

title: Mahābhārata Śalya Parva
description: The ninth book (Śalya Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the final day of war under Śalya's command, the mace duel between Bhīma and Duryodhana, and the end of the war.

title: Mahābhārata Strī Parva
description: The eleventh book (Strī Parva) of the Mahābhārata, depicting the lamentations of the women (strī) after the war, including Gandhārī's curse and the grief of the widows.

title: Mahābhārata Svargārohaṇa Parva
description: The seventeenth book (Svargārohaṇa Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing Yudhiṣṭhira's final ascent to heaven (svarga) and the resolution of the epic's central tensions.

title: Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva
description: The fifth book (Udyoga Parva) of the Mahābhārata, detailing the preparations for war (udyoga), the failed peace missions, and the marshalling of armies on both sides.

title: Mahābhārata Vana Parva
description: The third book (Vana Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the Pāṇḍavas' twelve-year exile in the forest (vana), their encounters with sages, and the Nala-Damayantī episode.

title: Mahābhārata Virāṭa Parva
description: The fourth book (Virāṭa Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the Pāṇḍavas' thirteenth year of exile incognito at the court of King Virāṭa.

title: Mahabharata
description: A sample record for a future guide to the Mahābhārata and its textual traditions. No translation or quotation is reproduced here.

title: Maitrāyaṇīya Āraṇyaka
description: The Maitrāyaṇīya Āraṇyaka, associated with the Maitrāyaṇīya Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, contains the Maitrī Upaniṣad and related forest-text material.

title: Maitrī Upaniṣad
description: The Maitrī Upaniṣad, associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda (Maitrāyaṇīya Śākhā), presents a dialogue between King Bṛhadratha and Sage Śākāyanya on the nature of the self and the means to liberation.

title: Makuṭa Āgama
description: The Makuṭa Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on the crown (makuṭa) of Śiva as the symbol of supreme sovereignty and the coronation rites of the liṅga.

title: Mānava Purāṇa
description: The Mānava Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, attributed to Manu, focusing on dharma, the four āśramas, and the worship of Viṣṇu.

title: Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad
description: The shortest principal Upaniṣad, focused on the syllable Oṃ and the four states of consciousness, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Manu Smṛti
description: The Manusmṛti (Mānava Dharmaśāstra), the most authoritative Dharmaśāstra text in twelve chapters, covering varṇa, āśrama, rājadharma, vyavahāra, prāyaścitta, and the rules of daily conduct.

title: Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa
description: The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in 137 chapters and ~9,000 verses, narrated as a dialogue between the sage Mārkaṇḍeya and Jaimini. Chapters 1-42: cosmology, creation, genealogies, the manvantaras; Chapters 43-80: the glory of the Sun (Sūrya), the legend of King Harishchandra; Chapters 81-93: the Devī Māhātmya (Durgā Saptashatī / Caṇḍī-pāṭha) — the Goddess's battles against Madhu-Kaiṭabha, Mahiṣāsura, and Śumbha-Niśumbha, the foundation of Śākta worship and Navarātrī; Chapters 94-137: the story of Dama, the glories of the Goddess, liberation through Devī-bhakti. The primary textual source for the Caṇḍī-pāṭha recited during Durgā Pūjā and Navarātrī across India, especially Bengal. ---

title: Matsya Purāṇa (Upapurāṇa)
description: The Matsya Upapurāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, distinct from the Mahāpurāṇa Matsya Purāṇa, focusing on the Matsya avatar of Viṣṇu, temple architecture, and vrata.

title: Matsya Purāṇa
description: The Matsya Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in ~14,000 verses and 291 chapters, narrated by Matsya (Viṣṇu's fish avatar) to Manu. Covers the Matsya avatāra and the flood legend, the seven Manus, royal genealogies (Sūryavaṃśa, Candravaṃśa), the five characteristics of a Purāṇa (pañca-lakṣaṇa), temple architecture (vāstu-śāstra: prāsāda, maṇḍapa, gopura, pratimā-lakṣaṇa), iconography of major deities, vrata rituals (Śivarātri, Caturmāsya, Ekādaśī), the Śrāddha-vidhi, the Prayāga-māhātmya, the Kāśī-māhātmya, and the Narmadā-māhātmya. The earliest Purāṇic source for Hindu temple architecture and iconography. ---

title: Mṛgendra Āgama
description: The Mṛgendra Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on the philosophy of Śiva, the nature of the soul (paśu), bondage (pāśa), and the path to liberation.

title: Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad distinguishing higher and lower knowledge, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Nandi Purāṇa
description: The Nandi Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, a Śaiva text narrated by Nandi (Śiva's bull), focusing on Śiva worship, the glory of the liṅga, and Śaiva rituals.

title: Nārada Purāṇa
description: The Nārada Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in two parts (Pūrvabhāga and Uttarabhāga) and ~25,000 verses, attributed to Nārada and narrated to the sages. Pūrvabhāga: the glory of Viṣṇu, the ten avatāras, the Gāyatrī-māhātmya, the Ekādaśī-vrata, the Śrāvaṇa-māsa-māhātmya, pilgrimage to Badarī, Dvārakā, Prayāga, Kāśī, Gayā; Uttarabhāga: the Bhakti-sūtras, the Nārada-bhakti-sūtra context, the Viṣṇu-sahasranāma, the Rāma-nāma-māhātmya, the glories of the Tulasī and Śālagrāma, the rules for Vaiṣṇava conduct (samayācāra). A comprehensive Vaiṣṇava dharma-śāstra and tīrtha-māhātmya text. ---

title: Nāradasmṛti
description: The Nāradasmṛti, a Dharmaśāstra text focused on vyavahāra (legal procedure), attributed to the sage Nārada.

title: Nṛsiṃha Purāṇa
description: The Nṛsiṃha Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, focusing on the Nṛsiṃha avatar of Viṣṇu, the story of Prahlāda, and the worship of Narasiṃha.

title: Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad
description: The Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad, a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad, identifies Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) as the supreme deity and teaches the dvādaśākṣara mantra.

title: Nāṭyaśāstra
description: The foundational treatise on performing arts attributed to Bharata Muni, covering drama, dance, music, and aesthetics.

title: Nighaṇṭu
description: The Nighaṇṭu is a collection of Vedic words arranged in thematic categories, serving as the lexical basis for Yāska's Nirukta.

title: Niḥśvāsa Āgama
description: The Niḥśvāsa Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, named for the "exhalation" (niḥśvāsa) of Śiva as the creative breath of the universe.

title: Nṛsiṃha Upapurāṇa
description: The Nṛsiṃha Upapurāṇa is one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, focusing on the Nṛsiṃha (man-lion) avatar of Viṣṇu. It contains stories of the devotee Prahlāda, the defeat of the demon Hiraṇyakaipu, and the symbolism of the Nṛsiṃha form as the Supreme Being who transcends all categories. The text also includes a description of the iconography, the sacred places associated with Nṛsiṃha worship, and the theological significance of the avatar. It is associated with the Vaiṣṇava tradition and is recited during the monthly Nṛsiṃha-vātaṇa and the annual Nṛsiṃha-jayantī festival. --- A subsidiary Purāṇa focusing on the Narasiṃha avatar, recited in Vaiṣṇava temples and household practice.

title: Nṛsiṃha Tāpanīya Purāṇa
description: The Nṛsiṃha Tāpanīya Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, a Vaiṣṇava text focusing on the Nṛsiṃha avatar, the Nṛsiṃha mantra, and the meditation on the fierce form of Viṣṇu.

title: Nṛsiṃha Upaniṣad
description: The Nṛsiṃha Upaniṣad, a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad associated with the Atharvaveda, focuses on the Nṛsiṃha avatar of Viṣṇu and the Nṛsiṃha mantra.

title: Padma Purāṇa
description: The Padma Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas, among the largest at ~55,000 verses in six khaṇḍas (Sṛṣṭi, Bhūmi, Svarga, Pātāla, Uttara, Kriyā-yoga). Organized around the lotus (padma) cosmology. Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa: creation, the glory of Puṣkara and other tīrthas; Bhūmi-khaṇḍa: earth geography, rivers, mountains, the Bhārata-varṣa; Svarga-khaṇḍa: heavens, the story of Rāma (Rāmāyaṇa summary), the glory of Ekādaśī; Pātāla-khaṇḍa: netherworlds, the story of Śeṣa, Viṣṇu's yoga-nidrā; Uttara-khaṇḍa: the essence of bhakti, the glory of Viṣṇu's names (Viṣṇu-sahasranāma context), pilgrimage to Brahmāvarta, Kāśī, Prayāga; Kriyā-yoga-khaṇḍa: temple rituals, vrata, dāna, the Puruṣottama-māhātmya (Jagannātha). Major source for tīrtha-māhātmya and Vaiṣṇava ritual.

title: Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa
description: The Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa (also Tāṇḍya Mahābrāhmaṇa), associated with the Kauthuma Śākhā of the Sāmaveda, contains twenty-five books of ritual instructions for soma sacrifices.

title: Aṣṭādhyāyī
description: The Aṣṭādhyāyī of Pāṇini is the foundational Sanskrit grammar text in sūtra form, systematizing Sanskrit morphology, syntax, and phonology.

title: Paramahaṃsa Upaniṣad
description: The Paramahaṃsa Upaniṣad, a saṃnyāsa Upaniṣad, describes the characteristics of the highest renouncer (paramahaṃsa) and the path of knowledge (jñāna).

title: Parameśvara Āgama
description: The Parameśvara Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, known for its detailed treatment of Śiva-Śakti philosophy, the nature of mala (impurity), and the path of initiation (dīkṣā).

title: Parāśarasmṛti
description: The Parāśarasmṛti, a Dharmaśāstra text attributed to the sage Parāśara, prescribing dharma for the Kali Yuga with emphasis on simplified rules.

title: Pauṣkara Saṃhitā
description: The Pauṣkara Saṃhitā, an important Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra text, detailing the fivefold daily worship (pañcakāla), the five forms of Viṣṇu, and the rituals of the arcāvatāra.

title: Praśna Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad organized around six questions, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Prodgītā Āgama
description: The Prodgītā Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, containing the "emerged song" (prodgītā) of Śiva, emphasizing the gītā (teaching song) format for conveying the highest Śaiva philosophy.

title: Rāmāyaṇa Araṇya Kāṇḍa
description: The third kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Araṇya Kāṇḍa), describing Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa's life in the forest, the encounter with Śūrpaṇakhā, and Sītā's abduction by Rāvaṇa.

title: Rāmāyaṇa Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa
description: The second kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa), describing the events in Ayodhyā leading to Rāma's exile, including Kaikeyī's boons, Daśaratha's grief, and Rāma's departure.

title: Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa
description: The first kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Bāla Kāṇḍa), describing the birth of Rāma, his childhood, education under Vasiṣṭha, marriage to Sītā, and the journey to Mithilā.

title: Rāmāyaṇa Kiṣkindhā Kāṇḍa
description: The fourth kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Kiṣkindhā Kāṇḍa), describing Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa's alliance with Sugrīva, the search for Sītā, and the killing of Vālin.

title: Rāmāyaṇa Sundara Kāṇḍa
description: The fifth kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Sundara Kāṇḍa), focusing on Hanumān's leap to Laṅkā, his meeting with Sītā, and the burning of Laṅkā.

title: Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa
description: The seventh kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Uttara Kāṇḍa), describing Rāma's return to Ayodhyā, his coronation, Sītā's banishment, the birth of his sons, and his eventual departure.

title: Rāmāyaṇa Yuddha Kāṇḍa
description: The sixth kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Yuddha Kāṇḍa), describing the war between Rāma's army and Rāvaṇa's forces, the death of Rāvaṇa, and Sītā's rescue.

title: Rāmāyaṇa
description: An Itihāsa text with many regional and textual traditions. This record avoids collapsing those traditions into one account.

title: Raurava Āgama
description: The Raurava Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, known for its detailed treatment of temple architecture, iconography, and the philosophy of Śiva-Śakti.

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 1
description: The first Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 191 hymns (sūktas) primarily dedicated to Agni and Indra; its composition is attributed to the ṛṣi Madhucchandas and other seers.

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 10
description: The tenth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 191 hymns attributed to various ṛṣis; contains the Puruṣa Sūkta (10.90), Nāsadīya Sūkta (10.129), and hymns on cosmology, philosophy, and social life.

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 2
description: Mandala II of the Ṛg Veda centres on the Āditya family: Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, and the twin deities (Mitra-twins) of cosmic order (ṛta). Its hymns (especially the Varuṇa and Mitra sūktas) articulate the moral and cosmic dimensions of the Vedic conception of law, the guest-sacrament (atithya), and the early 'contract' theology (mitāṅkatā). The mandala preserves the oldest formulation of the 'two paths' (dvayi-vāk) and the earliest allusions to the sacrifice (yajña) as the cosmogonic act.

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 3
description: Mandala III of the Ṛg Vāda, the 'Viṣṇu-mandala,' glorifies the three steps (trivandhura) of the Boar and the cosmic-measurement (puru-māṇḍala) of Viṣṇu, the god who 'stepped beyond' (adhyātman) the universe. The Viṣṇu sūktas (particularly the celebrated 'viṣṇor neto jyāyās tvag' and 'saṃprasthena triguṇena') articulate the Vedic conception of divine immanence and transcendence and are later the scriptural warrant for the Vaiṣṇṇava theology of the avatar.

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 4
description: Mandala IV of the Ṛg Veda, the 'Agni-mandala,' is dominated by hymns to Agni (the fire-god and the personification of the sacrificial oblation) and to the Maruts (the storm-gods of the atmospheric class). Its hymns describe Agni as the Hotṛ (priest of the sacrifice), the divine messenger who conveys the offerings to the gods, and the witness of oaths (dṛu). The Mandala's structure reflects the centrality of the ritual fire (yajña) in the early Vedic household and the sacral kingship (rājā) it secures.

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 5
description: Mandala V of the Ṛg Veda, the 'Aindra-mandala,' preserves hymns to Indra (the Vedic king of the gods and the destroyer of Vṛtra), the Maruts, and the Āditya Varuṇa. The Indra-hymns (especially the 'Hymn to Viśve Devāḥ' and the famous 'Indra-vad') portray Indra as the wielder of thunder and the conqueror of the mountain and the serpent. This Mandala is the locus of the early Vedic 'heroic' theology that makes the sacrifice (yajña) and the soma-drink the condition of victory over chaos.

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 6
description: Mandala VI of the Ṛg Veda, named after the sage Gotama Āraṇya, is the 'Āraṇya-mandala' and the last of the 'family books' (kula-sūktas). It contains the famous 'Hymn of the Two Paths' (dvayi-vāk) of the sage of the two ways, the early formulation of the doctrine of the three worlds, and the hymn to the Asvins. Mandala VI is a source for the earliest Indian medicine (āyurveda) and the first glimpses of the 'worldly' (laukika) concerns of the later Vedic ritual.

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 7
description: The seventh Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 104 hymns attributed to the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha; dedicated to Indra, Agni, Varuṇa, and the Viśvedevas; contains the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya Mantra (7.59.12).

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 8
description: The eighth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 103 hymns attributed to the Kaṇva and Āṅgirasa families; dedicated to Indra, Agni, and the Aśvins; contains the Vālakhilya hymns (8.49–59).

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 9
description: The ninth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 114 hymns dedicated entirely to Soma Pavamāna (the purifying Soma); its hymns are attributed to various ṛṣis and are used in the Soma sacrifice.

title: Ṛgveda Saṃhitā
description: The Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, the oldest Vedic collection of 1028 hymns (sūktas) in ten maṇḍalas, dedicated to various deities.

title: Rigveda
description: The Ṛg Veda (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā) is the oldest extant Indo-European text (c. 1500–1200 BCE), the first of the four Vedas, containing 1028 hymns (sūktas) in diverse meters. It preserves the oldest attested Indian religious poetry addressed to the Vedic deities (Indra, Agni, Varuṇa, the Ādityas, the Viśvedevas). The Ṛg is cited as the 'earliest testimony' (sākṣat) of the Dharmaśāstras and the source of the Gāyatrī-mantra (3.62.10). Its ten Mandalas (books) are organized around the cosmic order (ṛta); the Ṛg is the foundation of the Vedic ritual (yajña) and of later Indian philosophy (e.g. the puruṣa-sūkta of the tenth Mandala).

title: Rudra Āgama
description: The Rudra Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on Rudra as the fierce and transformative aspect of Śiva, with detailed rites for the pacification (śānti) and propitiation of Rudra.

title: Rudrayāmala Tantra
description: The Rudrayāmala Tantra, a major Śākta-Śaiva Tantra in 44 chapters, expounding the worship of Śiva and Śakti in their fierce forms, the ten Mahāvidyās, and the practice of kaula.

title: Rudrahṛdaya Upaniṣad
description: The Rudrahṛdaya Upaniṣad, a Śaiva Upaniṣad, identifies Rudra as the supreme reality and the heart (hṛdaya) of all beings.

title: Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāhmaṇa
description: The Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, the twenty-sixth book supplementing the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, contains additional ritual material for Sāma Vedic sacrifices.

title: Sahasra Āgama
description: The Sahasra Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, named for its thousand (sahasra) verses or topics, covering all four pādas with emphasis on the thousand names and forms of Śiva.

title: Sāmaveda Āraṇyaka
description: The Sāmaveda Āraṇyakas, associated with the Kauthuma and Jaiminīya Śākhās, contain the Chāndogya Upaniṣad and related forest texts.

title: Sāmaveda Saṃhitā
description: The Sāmaveda Saṃhitā is the collection of melodic verses (sāmans) drawn primarily from the Ṛgveda for liturgical chanting.

title: Sāmaveda
description: The Sāmaveda ('Veda of melodies') is the Vedic collection that preserves Ṛgvedic verses adapted into melodic (sāman) recitation for the soma-yajña; it is divided traditionally into a Pūrva (the earlier, melody-oriented texts drawn from the Ṛg) and a Uttara (the Āraṇyaka-like portions). Only two recensions (śākhas) survive: the Jaiminiya (the 'Jaiminiya Sāma') and the Śukla (the 'white' Sāma); their melodic (sāma-gāna) traditions differ from one another and from the plain (text) recitation of the other Vedas.

title: Sāmba Purāṇa
description: The Sāmba Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, narrated by Sāmba (Kṛṣṇa's son), focusing on Sūrya worship, the healing of Sāmba's leprosy through solar worship, and the solar temples of India.

title: Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka
description: The Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka, associated with the Ṛgveda, contains the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad and discusses the inner meaning of ritual.

title: Śāṅkhāyana Brāhmaṇa
description: The Śāṅkhāyana Brāhmaṇa (also Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa), associated with the Bāṣkala Śākhā of the Ṛgveda; contains ritual prescriptions and theological explanations.

title: Sarvokta Āgama
description: The Sarvokta Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, known for its comprehensive treatment of the four pādas and its influence on temple architecture in South India.

title: Sāttvata Saṃhitā
description: The Sāttvata Saṃhitā, an early Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra text, detailing the five forms of Viṣṇu, the cakra system, and the rituals of temple worship.

title: Saura Purāṇa
description: The Saura Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, focusing on the worship of Sūrya (the Sun), solar cosmology, and the Sūrya mantras.

title: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa
description: The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, associated with the Mādhyandina and Kāṇva Śākhās of the Śukla Yajurveda, is one of the most extensive Brāhmaṇas, containing detailed ritual instructions and theological discussions including the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad.

title: Śiva Purāṇa
description: The Śiva Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in seven saṃhitās (Vidyeśvara, Rudra, Śatarudra, Koṭirudra, Umā, Kailāsa, Vāyavīya) and ~24,000 verses. Saṃhitā 1 (Vidyeśvara): glory of Śiva, liṅga worship, jyotirliṅgas; Saṃhitā 2 (Rudra): Rudra's forms, the eleven Rudras; Saṃhitā 3 (Śatarudra): hundred names of Rudra, Śiva's cosmic dance; Saṃhitā 4 (Koṭirudra): twelve jyotirliṅgas (Somnath, Mallikārjuna, Mahākāleśvara, Omkāreśvara, Kedārnāth, Bhīmaśaṅkar, Viśvanāth, Tryambakeśvara, Vaidyanāth, Nāgeśvara, Rāmeśvara, Ghṛṣṇeśvara); Saṃhitā 5 (Umā): Pārvatī's birth, marriage, Gaṇeśa, Skanda; Saṃhitā 6 (Kailāsa): Kailāsa, the yoga of Śiva, the five faces; Saṃhitā 7 (Vāyavīya): Vāyu's narration, the Śiva-gītā, liberation through Śiva-bhakti. Central to Śaiva Siddhānta and temple traditions. ---

title: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad
description: The Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad, associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, is a theistic Upaniṣad focusing on Rudra/Śiva as the supreme deity.

title: Skanda Purāṇa
aliases: ச கந ட ப ர ணம்
description: The Skanda Purāṇa, the largest Mahāpurāṇa at ~81,000+ verses in seven khaṇḍas (Māheśvara, Viṣṇu, Brahma, Kāśī, Āvantya, Nāgara, Prabhāsa). Māheśvara-khaṇḍa: Śiva's glory, the twelve jyotirliṅgas, Kedāra-khaṇḍa (Himalayan tīrthas); Viṣṇu-khaṇḍa: Viṣṇu avatāras, Badarī, Puruṣottama (Jagannātha); Brahma-khaṇḍa: creation, Brahmā's life, Puṣkara, Gayā; Kāśī-khaṇḍa: Kāśī/Avimiukta, the glory of Kāśī, the Annapūrṇā temple; Āvantya-khaṇḍa: Avantī/Ujjayinī, Mahākāleśvara, the Siṃhastha Kumbha; Nāgara-khaṇḍa: Gujarat tīrthas, Dvārakā, Prabhāsa; Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa: Somnāth, the Yādava dynasty, the end of Kṛṣṇa's līlā. The definitive tīrtha-māhātmya text for Śaiva and pan-Hindu pilgrimage. ---

title: Subāla Upaniṣad
description: The Subāla Upaniṣad, associated with the Śukla Yajurveda, is a dialogue between Sage Subāla and Prajāpati on the nature of Brahman, the self, and the universe.

title: Sūkṣma Āgama
description: The Sūkṣma Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on the subtle (sūkṣma) body, the nāḍīs, cakras, and the kuṇḍalinī yoga leading to Śiva-realization.

title: Suprabheda Āgama
description: The Suprabheda Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, covering jñāna, yoga, kriyā, and caryā pādas with emphasis on temple construction and iconography.

title: Svāyambhuva Āgama
description: The Svāyambhuva Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, attributed to Svāyambhuva Manu, emphasizing the self-born (svayambhu) nature of Śiva as the uncreated source.

title: Taittirīya Āraṇyaka
description: The Taittirīya Āraṇyaka, associated with the Taittirīya Śākhā, contains the Taittirīya Upaniṣad and the Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad.

title: Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa
description: The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, associated with the Taittirīya Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, provides ritual explanations and theological interpretations of the Saṃhitā mantras.

title: Taittirīya Saṃhitā
description: The Taittirīya Saṃhitā is the Saṃhitā of the Taittirīya Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, containing mantras for Vedic rituals.

title: Taittirīya Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Tārasāra Upaniṣad
description: The Tārasāra Upaniṣad, a Śaiva Upaniṣad, identifies Rudra as the supreme reality and the heart (hṛdaya) of all beings.

title: Tripurā Rahasya
description: The Tripurā Rahasya, a Śākta text in three books (Mahātmya, Jñāna, Caryā), attributed to Dattātreya, expounding the worship of Tripurasundarī, the nature of consciousness, and the path of jñāna within the Śrīvidyā tradition.

title: Madhusūdana Sarasvatī Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas
description: Madhusūdana Sarasvatī's Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas (especially on the Īśa, Kaṭha, and Bṛhadāraṇyaka), a 16th-century Advaita scholar's synthesis of Śaṅkara's Advaita with Bhakti.

title: Madhva Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas
description: Madhva's commentaries on the ten principal Upaniṣads, presenting the Dvaita interpretation of the mahāvākyas, the eternal distinction between jīva and Brahman, and the role of bhakti.

title: Rāmānanda Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas
description: Rāmānanda's Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas, reflecting the Viśiṣṭādvaita tradition in the North Indian Bhakti context, emphasizing Rāma as the supreme reality of the Upaniṣads.

title: Rāmānuja Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas
description: Rāmānuja's commentaries on selected Upaniṣads (including the Vedārtha Saṅgraha, a summary of Upaniṣadic teaching), presenting the Viśiṣṭādvaita interpretation of Brahman as qualified by cit and acit.

title: Śaṅkara Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas
description: Śaṅkara's commentaries on the ten principal Upaniṣads (Īśa, Kena, Kaṭha, Praśna, Muṇḍaka, Māṇḍūkya, Taittirīya, Aitareya, Chāndogya, Bṛhadāraṇyaka).

title: Vallabha Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas
description: Vallabha's commentaries on selected Upaniṣads (including the Subodhinī on the Īśa, Kaṭha, and Bṛhadāraṇyaka), presenting the Śuddhādvaita interpretation and the path of puṣṭi (grace).

title: Vāmana Purāṇa
description: The Vāmana Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in 95 chapters and ~10,000 verses, narrated by Pulastya to Nārada. Focuses on Viṣṇu's Vāmana avatāra, the Bali-Vāmana narrative (three strides covering the three worlds), and the tīrthas of Kurukṣetra. Also covers: the Dakṣa-yajña and Śiva's destruction of it, the birth of Gaṅgā, the Sarasvatī-māhātmya, the Yamunā-māhātmya, the Gayā-śrāddha, the Prayāga-māhātmya, the Kāśī-māhātmya, and the glories of the Nṛsiṃha avatāra. A key text for Kurukṣetra pilgrimage and the Vāmana-Nṛsiṃha dual focus of Viṣṇu worship. ---

title: Varāha Purāṇa (Upapurāṇa)
description: The Varāha Upapurāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, distinct from the Mahāpurāṇa Varāha Purāṇa, focusing on Viṣṇu's Varāha avatar and the rescue of Bhūdevī.

title: Varāha Purāṇa
description: The Varāha Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in 217 chapters and ~24,000 verses, narrated by Varāha (Viṣṇu's boar avatar) to Bhūdevī. Focuses on tīrthas (pilgrimage sites), vrata (vows), and Viṣṇu-bhakti. Major sections: the rescue of Bhūdevī, the Varāha-kṣetra (Tirupati), the Śrīveṅkaṭeśa-māhātmya, the Badarī-kṣetra, the Puṣkara-māhātmya, the Gayā-śrāddha-vidhi, the Mathurā-māhātmya, the Dvārakā-māhātmya, the Kāśī-māhātmya, the Prayāga-māhātmya, and numerous vrata-kathās (Śrāvaṇa, Kārtika, Mārgaśīrṣa). The most detailed tīrtha-māhātmya text among the Purāṇas for North and Central Indian Vaiṣṇava sites. ---

title: Vārttika
description: The Vārttikas of Kātyāyana are critical supplements to Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī, identifying omissions, redundancies, and errors.

title: Vasiṣṭha Dharmasūtra
description: An early Dharmasūtra associated with the Ṛgveda, prescribing duties for the four varṇas and āśramas.

title: Vāsudeva Upaniṣad
description: The Vāsudeva Upaniṣad, a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad associated with the Saṃhitā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, focuses on Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa) as the supreme deity and the dvādaśākṣara mantra.

title: Vātula Āgama
description: The Vātula Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, a text of the Vātula Śaiva tradition, covering the four pādas with emphasis on yoga and the nature of Śiva as the supreme reality.

title: Vāyu Purāṇa
description: The Vāyu Purāṇa, a Śaiva Mahāpurāṇa in four padas (prakriyā, anuṣaṅga, upodghāta, upasaṃhāra) and ~24,000 verses, narrated by Vāyu to the sages. Covers creation cycles, the kalpas and manvantaras, the genealogies of kings and sages (sūryavaṃśa, candravaṃśa), the geography of the seven dvīpas and Bhārata-varṣa, the Śiva kṣetras (Kāśī, Gayā, Puṣkara, Śrīśaila, Kedāra), the Aṣṭādaśa-śakti-pīṭhas, the Gayā-māhātmya and the Śrāddha-vidhi. Closely related to the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (shares the Lalitopākhyāna and Āditya-hṛdaya). Preserves the early Śaiva cosmology and the genealogical tradition of the Purāṇas. ---

title: Vijaya Āgama
description: The Vijaya Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, emphasizing the victorious (vijaya) path of Śiva-worship leading to liberation, with detailed kriyā and caryā sections for temple and home worship.

title: Vīra Āgama
description: The Vīra Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, associated with the Vīra Śaiva tradition, covering the four pādas with emphasis on the vīra (heroic) path of Śiva worship.

title: Viṣṇu Dharmottara Purāṇa
description: The Viṣṇu Dharmottara Purāṇa, a major Upapurāṇa supplementing the Viṣṇu Purāṇa, covering temple architecture (vāstu), iconography (pratimā-lakṣaṇa), painting (citra), dance (nṛtya), and the Viṣṇu bhakti tradition.

title: Viṣṇu Purāṇa
description: The Viṣṇu Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in six aṃśas (parts) and ~23,000 verses, attributed to Parāśara and narrated to Maitreya. Aṃśa 1: creation (sarga), cosmology, the varṇāśrama system; Aṃśa 2: geography (dvīpas, varṣas), Pātāla, hells, the seven dvīpas; Aṃśa 3: Manus, manvantaras, the solar and lunar dynasties (Sūryavaṃśa, Candravaṃśa); Aṃśa 4: detailed genealogies of kings through the ages; Aṃśa 5: Kṛṣṇa's life (Mathurā, Vṛndāvana, Dvārakā, Jarāsandha, Kālayavana, the Pāṇḍavas); Aṃśa 6: dissolution (pralaya), the path of liberation, the glories of Viṣṇu-bhakti. The earliest and most systematic Vaiṣṇava Purāṇa, foundational for later bhakti traditions. ---

title: Mahābhāṣya
description: The Mahābhāṣya of Patañjali is the major commentary on Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī, providing extensive grammatical analysis and philosophical discussion.

title: Vyāsasmṛti
description: The Vyāsasmṛti, a Dharmaśāstra text attributed to Vyāsa, dealing with ācāra, vyavahāra, and prāyaścitta.

title: Yājñavalkya Smṛti
description: The Yājñavalkya Smṛti, a systematic Dharmaśāstra text in three books (ācāra, vyavahāra, prāyaścitta), more concise and organized than Manusmṛti.

title: Yajurveda Saṃhitā
description: The Yajurveda Saṃhitā, the collection of prose mantras (yajus) for ritual use, transmitted in Kṛṣṇa (Taittirīya, Maitrāyaṇīya, Kaṭha, Kāpiṣṭhala) and Śukla (Mādhyandina, Kāṇva) recensions.

title: Yajurveda
description: A Vedic collection represented here as a concise catalogue record. Its recensions and associated textual layers require context-specific study.

title: Yāska's Nirukta
description: The Nirukta, attributed to Yāska, is the Vedāṅga of etymology and semantic interpretation, providing explanations of obscure Vedic terms through derivations and glosses.

title: Yoga Sūtra
description: The Yoga Sūtra of Patañjali (c. 2nd–4th century CE), the foundational text of classical Yoga darśana, in four pādas (samādhi, sādhana, vibhūti, kaivalya) and 195 sūtras.

title: Yogacūḍāmaṇi Upaniṣad
description: The Yogacūḍāmaṇi Upaniṣad, a Yoga Upaniṣad, describes the chakras, nāḍīs, kuṇḍalinī, and the practice of rāja-yoga leading to samādhi.

title: Yogajā Āgama
description: The Yogajā Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, emphasizing the yoga pāda and the union of the individual soul (paśu) with Śiva through the eight limbs of yoga.

title: Yogatattva Upaniṣad
description: The Yogatattva Upaniṣad, a Yoga Upaniṣad, classifies yoga into mantra, laya, haṭha, and rāja yoga, and describes the four stages of yoga practice.

title: Ahobilam Divya Deśam
description: The Nava Narasiṃha Temple complex at Ahobilam (Nandyal district, Andhra Pradesh), a Divya Deśam with nine shrines for the nine forms of Narasiṃha (Nava Narasiṃha): Ahobila, Bhārgava, Yogananda, Chatravata, Krodha, Malola, Jvālā, Pavana, and Karanja. Spread across the Nallamala Hills. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār and Nammāḻvār. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Narasiṃha-jayantī attract thousands. Unique for the nine distinct Narasiṃha forms in one pilgrimage circuit. ---

title: Akshardham Delhi
description: The Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple in Delhi, a modern stone temple complex (completed 2005) built by BAPS, dedicated to Bhagavān Swaminarayan.

title: Aḻagar Kōyil Temple
description: The Aḻagar Kōyil Temple near Madurai (Tamil Nadu), one of the 108 Divya Deśams, dedicated to Kallāḻagar (Viṣṇu as Kallāḻagar).

title: Aṣṭabhujākaram Divya Deśam
description: The Aṣṭabhujākaram Temple (Eight-armed Viṣṇu) at Kāñcīpuram (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu with eight arms (aṣṭa-bhuja) holding the conch, discus, mace, lotus, bow, arrow, sword, and shield. The Cōḷa-period temple where Viṣṇu appeared to the sage Bhṛgu. Glorified by Poygai Āḻvār, Bhūta Āḻvār, Pēy Āḻvār, and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Bhṛgu-pūjā are celebrated. One of the cluster of Kāñcī Divya Deśams. ---

title: Badrinath Divya Deśam
description: The Badrinath Temple (Badarīnātha), a Divya Deśam in the Garhwal Himalayas (Uttarakhand) at 3,133 m, dedicated to Viṣṇu as Badarīnārāyaṇa. One of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites and one of the 108 Divya Deśams glorified by the Āḻvārs (Nammāḻvār, Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār). The temple houses a 1m black stone image of Viṣṇu in padmāsana. Open only six months a year (Apr-Nov); the idol is moved to Joshimath in winter. Mentioned in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham. ---

title: Baidyanath Temple
description: The Baidyanath Temple at Deoghar (Jharkhand), one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas, also known as Baba Baidyanath Dham, where Rāvaṇa is said to have worshipped Śiva.

title: Belur Chennakesava Temple
description: The Chennakesava Temple at Belur, Karnataka, a Hoysala masterpiece with intricate soapstone sculptures, built by Viṣṇuvardhana.

title: Bṛhadīśvara Temple (Tanjore)
description: The Bṛhadīśvara Temple at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, a UNESCO World Heritage site built by Rājarāja I.

title: Chamunda Devi Temple
description: The Chāmuṇḍā Devī Temple in Himachal Pradesh, one of the fifty-one Śakti Pīṭhas, where the feet of Devī fell, dedicated to the fierce form Chāmuṇḍā.

title: Chidambaram Nataraja Temple
description: The Naṭarāja Temple at Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu, dedicated to Śiva as the cosmic dancer (Naṭarāja).

title: Dakṣiṇeśvara Kālī Temple
description: The Dakṣiṇeśvara Kālī Temple near Kolkata (West Bengal), built by Rāṇī Rashmoni, where Rāmakṛṣṇa Paramahaṃsa attained spiritual realization.

title: Devaprayāga Divya Deśam
description: The Raghunāthajī Temple at Devaprayāga (Tehri Garhwal, Uttarakhand), a Divya Deśam at the confluence of the Alaknandā and Bhāgīrathī (forming the Gaṅgā). Dedicated to Viṣṇu as Raghunāthajī (Rāma). The legendary spot where Rāma performed penance after the Rāvaṇa war. The temple was rebuilt by the Garhwal kings. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Rāma-navamī and the Gaṅgā-avataraṇa (Gaṅgā descent) festivals are celebrated. One of the five Prayāga confluences. ---

title: Dvārakā Temple (Dvārakādhīśa)
description: The Dvārakādhīśa Temple at Dvārakā, Gujarat, one of the four Dhāmas and a major Kṛṣṇa pilgrimage site.

title: Dvārakā Divya Deśam
description: The Dvārakādhīśa Temple (Dvārakā), a Divya Deśam on the Gujarat coast, dedicated to Viṣṇu as Dvārakādhīśa (Lord of Dvārakā). One of the four Char Dham and one of the 108 Divya Deśams. The original temple is attributed to Vajranābha (Kṛṣṇa's great-grandson); the current structure dates to 15th-16th century. The five-storey śikhara rises 78m. Glorified by Nammāḻvār and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham. The Kṛṣṇa janmabhūmi and the nearby Bet Dwarka (Śāṇṭipura) are associated sites. ---

title: Dvārakā Maṭha
description: The Dvārakā Śāradā Pīṭham (Dvārakā Maṭha) in Gujarat, the second of the four Ādi Śaṅkara maṭhas, dedicated to Śāradā.

title: Ekambareswarar Temple Kanchipuram
description: The Ekambareśvarar Temple at Kāñcīpuram, Tamil Nadu, one of the Pañcabhūta-sthalas representing earth (pṛthvī).

title: Gṛhṇeśvara Temple
description: The Gṛhṇeśvara Temple near Ellora (Maharashtra), the twelfth of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas, located near the Ellora Caves (UNESCO World Heritage site).

title: Guruvāyūr Temple (Kṛṣṇa)
description: The Guruvāyūr Temple (ഗുരുവായൂര്‍ / குருவாயூர்) in Thrissur district, Kerala — "Bhūloka Vaikuṇṭha" (Vaikuṇṭha on Earth). Dedicated to Kṛṣṇa as Guruvāyūrapurṇan (the Lord of Guruvāyūr), a four-armed standing Viṣṇu with conch, discus, mace, lotus. The idol is said to be worshipped by Vāyu and Bṛhaspati (hence Guru-vāyūr). Kerala architecture: copper-plated roof, golden flagstaff (dvaja-stambha), the Chuttambalam (circumambulatory). Famous for elephants (Punnathur Kotta — elephant sanctuary), the daily uṣa-pūjā (3:30 AM), and the Guruvāyūr Śrī Kṛṣṇa Suprabhātam. The annual Ekādaśī (Vṛścika Ekādaśī, Nov-Dec) and the Utsavam (festival, Feb-Mar) with the Āna-yoṭṭam (elephant race) draw millions. The temple's unique appam-prasādam (rice cake) and the Guruvāyūr Devaswom management.

title: Halebidu Hoysaleswara Temple
description: The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu, Karnataka, a twin Hoysala temple dedicated to Śiva, renowned for its extensive sculptural program.

title: Jagannātha Purī Divya Deśam
description: The Jagannātha Temple at Purī (Odisha), a Divya Deśam and one of the four Char Dham, dedicated to Viṣṇu as Jagannātha (Lord of the Universe) with Balabhadra and Subhadrā. The iconic wooden deities are renewed every 12-19 years (Nabakalebara). The massive Ratha-yātrā festival draws millions. Glorified by all twelve Āḻvārs in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham. The temple kitchen (Mahāprasāda) serves 10,000+ daily. The Govardhana-maṭha of Śaṅkara is located here. ---

title: Jagannātha Temple, Purī
description: The Jagannātha Temple at Purī, Odisha, one of the four Dhāmas.

title: Jambukeswarar Temple Tiruvanaikaval
description: The Jambukeśvarar Temple at Tiruvanaikaval (near Tiruchirappalli), Tamil Nadu, one of the Pañcabhūta-sthalas representing water (āpas/jala).

title: Jyotirmaṭha Divya Deśam
description: The Narasiṃha Temple at Jyotirmaṭha (Joshimath, Uttarakhand), a Divya Deśam and the winter seat of the Badrinath deity. Dedicated to Viṣṇu as Narasiṃha (the man-lion avatāra). One of the four Maṭhas established by Ādi Śaṅkara (the Uttara Maṭha). The deity is believed to be self-manifested (svayambhū). The temple is at 1,890m elevation. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Narasiṃha-jayantī and the Badrinath opening/closing ceremonies are centered here. The nearby Kalpavṛkṣa and the cave of Ādi Śaṅkara are pilgrimage sites. ---

title: Jvālāmukhī Temple
description: The Jvālāmukhī Temple in Kangra (Himachal Pradesh), one of the fifty-one Śakti Pīṭhas, where the tongue of Devī fell, famous for the eternal flame (jvālā) emerging from the rock.

title: Jyotir Maṭha
description: The Jyotir Maṭha (Jyotirmath/Joshimath) in Uttarakhand, the third of the four Ādi Śaṅkara maṭhas, located near Badrinath.

title: Kailāsa Giri Divya Deśam
description: The Kailāsa Giri Temple at Kailāsa Giri hills (Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Nārāyaṇa in a reclining posture (aśṭāṅgābhiṣeka form). The temple is built into the hillside. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Nārāyaṇa Ekādaśī are celebrated. Glorified by Tiruppaṇ Āḻvār. The temple offers panoramic views of the surrounding hills and plains. ---

title: Kālīghāṭ Temple Kolkata
description: The Kālīghāṭ Temple in Kolkata (West Bengal), one of the fifty-one Śakti Pīṭhas, where the right toe of Devī fell, a major center of Kālī worship.

title: Kāmākhyā Temple Guwahati
description: The Kāmākhyā Temple at Guwahati (Assam), one of the fifty-one Śakti Pīṭhas, where the yoni of Devī fell, a major center of Tantric Śākta worship.

title: Kāñcī Kāmakōṭi Pīṭham
description: The Kāñcī Kāmakōṭi Pīṭham at Kāñcīpuram, Tamil Nadu, a prominent Śaṅkara maṭha (though its direct Śaṅkara lineage is debated), dedicated to Kāmākṣī.

title: Kāñcī Varadarāja Perumal Divya Deśam
description: The Varadarāja Perumal Temple (Devarāja-svāmī) at Kāñcīpuram (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Varadarāja (the King who grants boons). The 11th-century Cōḷa structure with a 100-pillar mandapa and the Athi Varadar (the original wooden deity) preserved in the temple tank. Glorified by Nammāḻvār, Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār, Poygai Āḻvār, and Bhūta Āḻvār. One of the Kāñcī Divya Deśams along with Yathothkāri, Ulagalantha Perumal, and others. The Garuḍa-sevā festival is famous. ---

title: Kāñcīpuram Temples
description: The temple city of Kāñcīpuram, Tamil Nadu, with major Śaiva (Ekāmranātha, Kāmākṣī) and Vaiṣṇava (Varadarāja) temples.

title: Kāśī Viśvanātha Temple
description: The Viśvanātha Temple at Kāśī (Vārāṇasī), Uttar Pradesh, one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas and a major Śiva pilgrimage center.

title: Kedārnātha Temple
description: The Kedārnātha Temple at Kedarnath, Uttarakhand, one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas.

title: Khajuraho Temples
description: The Khajuraho group of temples, Madhya Pradesh, built by the Chandela dynasty (9th–12th centuries), famous for their erotic sculptures and Nagara architecture.

title: Konark Sun Temple
description: The Sun Temple at Konark, Odisha, a 13th-century chariot-shaped temple dedicated to Sūrya, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

title: Lingaraj Temple Bhubaneswar
description: The Lingarāja Temple at Bhubaneswar, Odisha, the largest temple in the city, dedicated to Harihara (Śiva-Viṣṇu composite).

title: Mahākāleśvara Temple Ujjain
description: The Mahākāleśvara Temple at Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas, unique for its south-facing (dakṣiṇāmukhī) liṅga and the Bhasma Ārati ritual.

title: Mīnākṣī Amman Temple
description: The Mīnākṣī Amman Temple at Madurai, Tamil Nadu, a major Śaiva-Śākta pilgrimage site with towering gopurams and tank.

title: Mukteshwar Temple Bhubaneswar
description: The Mukteśvara Temple at Bhubaneswar, Odisha, a 10th-century gem of Kalinga architecture, dedicated to Śiva as Mukteśvara (Lord of Liberation).

title: Nācciyār Kōyil Divya Deśam
description: The Nācciyār Kōyil (Tirunāṟaiyūr) at Tiruppanandal near Kumbakonam (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Śrīnivāsa Perumāl with Goddess Nācciyār (Lakṣmī). The Cōḷa-period temple where Lakṣmī is enshrined as the primary deity (Nācciyār) — unique among Divya Deśams. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār and Nammāḻvār. The annual Garuḍa-sevā and the Tiruppāvai festival (Mārgaḻi) are celebrated. The temple architecture follows the madhyama (medium) type. ---

title: Nāgeśvara Temple Dwarka
description: The Nāgeśvara Temple near Dwarka (Gujarat), one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas, located near the Dwarkadhish Temple.

title: Naṅguṇeri Divya Deśam
description: The Vanamāmalai (Tōṭādṛ) Temple at Naṅguṇeri (Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Vaṉamāmalai (the Lord of the forest garland). The headquarters of the Vaṉamāmalai Maṭha (a Śrīvaiṣṇava monastery). The 15th-century temple with a 100-pillar mandapa and beautiful bronzes. Glorified by Nammāḻvār and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Vaṉamāmalai Maṭha's festivals are celebrated. An important center for Śrīvaiṣṇava theology and Sanskrit learning. ---

title: Omkāreśvara Temple
description: The Omkāreśvara Temple on Mandhata Island (Madhya Pradesh), one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas, situated on the Narmadā river, with the unique Om-shaped island.

title: Oppiliappan Divya Deśam
description: The Oppiliappan Temple (Uppiliappan) near Kumbakonam (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Oppiliappan (the Lord who accepts even saltless offerings). The legend: Lakṣmī as Bhūmidevi offered food without salt; Viṣṇu accepted it, hence "Uppu-illa-appan" (Lord without salt). No salt is used in the temple kitchen. Glorified by Nammāḻvār and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple tank (Tula-puṣkariṇī) and the annual Pavitrotsavam are notable. ---

title: Pāṇḍharpur Temple (Viṭṭhala)
description: The Viṭṭhala Temple at Pāṇḍharpur, Maharashtra, the center of the Vārkarī tradition.

title: Purī Govardhana Maṭha
description: The Purī Govardhana Maṭha in Odisha, the fourth of the four Ādi Śaṅkara maṭhas, dedicated to Jagannātha.

title: Rāmeśvaram Divya Deśam
description: The Rāmanāthasvāmī Temple at Rāmeśvaram (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam and one of the four Char Dham, dedicated to Viṣṇu as Rāmanātha (Rāma's Lord) — here Viṣṇu and Śiva are worshipped together. One of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas (Rāmanāthaliṅga). The longest temple corridor in India (1,220m with 1,212 pillars). Glorified by Nammāḻvār, Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār, and Kulasekhara Āḻvār. The sacred tīrthas (22 wells) within the complex. The Sethu (Adam's Bridge) to Śrī Lanka is nearby. ---

title: Sabarimala Temple (Ayyappa)
description: The Ayyappa Temple at Sabarimala (ശബരിമല / சபரிமலை), Kerala, in the Periyar Tiger Reserve (Western Ghats) at 914m elevation. A major pilgrimage site (40-50 million annually, Nov-Jan) with a distinctive 41-day vrata (maṇḍala kālam / മണ്ഡല കാലം): black/blue clothes, brahmacarya, daily bath, no shaving, no footwear, vegetarian diet. The 18 holy steps (paṭinēṭṭāmpaṭi / பதினெட்டாம்படி) represent the 18 purāṇas/18 guṇas; only those carrying the irumuḍi (sacred bundle) may ascend. The deity is a yogic Śāstā in chin-mudrā. Makaravilakku (Makara Jyoti) on Makara Saṅkrānti (Jan 14/15) is the climax. The Vāvaru (Muslim devotee) shrine at Erumeli and the Peta (Petty) shrine en route exemplify communal harmony. The river Pampa is the sacred bathing ghāṭ. Managed by the Travancore Devaswom Board.

title: Śrīraṅgam Sāraṅgāpani Divya Deśam
description: The Sāraṅgāpani Temple at Kumbakonam (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Sāraṅgāpani (holding the bow Sāraṅga). The 12th-century Cōḷa temple with a 50m tall gopura and the unique chariot-shaped (ratha) sanctum. The chariot festival (Rathotsava) is famous. Glorified by Nammāḻvār, Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār, Poygai Āḻvār, and Periyalvār. The temple tank (Hema-puṣkariṇī) is sacred. One of the five Pañcarātra temples (with Śrīraṅgam, Tirupati, Kāñcī, and Badrinath). ---

title: Śṛṅgerī Maṭha
description: The Śṛṅgerī Śāradā Pīṭham (Śṛṅgerī Maṭha) in Karnataka, the first of the four Ādi Śaṅkara maṭhas, dedicated to Śāradā (Sarasvatī).

title: Simhācalam Divya Deśam
description: The Varāha Narasiṃha Temple at Simhācalam (Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Varāha Narasiṃha (the boar-man-lion form). The deity is covered in sandalwood paste year-round (revealed only on Akṣaya Tritīyā). The Kalinga-style architecture with a 96-pillar mandapa. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Candana-yātrā (sandalwood procession) and the Narasiṃha-jayantī are major festivals. One of the few Divya Deśams with a Narasiṃha primary deity. ---

title: Somnāth Temple
description: The Somnāth Temple at Prabhas Patan, Gujarat, the first of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas.

title: Śrīraṅgam Ranganatha Divya Deśam
description: The Śrī Raṅganātha Temple at Śrīraṅgam (Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu), the foremost Divya Deśam and the largest functioning Hindu temple complex (156 acres). Dedicated to Viṣṇu as Raṅganātha (reclining on Ādiśeṣa). Seven concentric prākāras, 21 gopuras (the Rājagopuram is 73m, Asia's tallest). The Āḻvār tradition: all twelve Āḻvārs glorified it; Nammāḻvār's Tiruvāymoḻi was first recited here. The annual Vaikuṇṭha Ekādaśī (21-day festival) draws millions. The temple houses the Āḻvār sannidhis and the Rāmānuja's sanctum. ---

title: Śrīvilliputtūr Āṇḍāl Temple
description: The Śrīvilliputtūr Temple, one of the 108 Divya Deśams, the birthplace of Āṇḍāl (the only female Āḻvār), dedicated to Vaṭapaṭraśāyī Perumal and Āṇḍāl.

title: Tiruccherapalli Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruccherapalli Temple at Tiruchirappalli (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tiruccherapalli Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the sacred place and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tirucitra Divya Deśam
description: The Tirucitrakoodal Temple (Citra-kūṭal) at Tiruninravur (near Chennai, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Viṣṇu (Citra-kūṭa Perumāl). The Cōḷa-period temple with beautiful bronze icons. The temple tank (Citra-puṣkariṇī) is associated with the legend of Citragupta. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Citragupta-pūjā are celebrated. A smaller but historically significant Divya Deśam. ---

title: Tirukāmākṣaṇa Divya Deśam
description: The Tirukāmākṣaṇa Temple (Thirukadambari) at Kumbakonam (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tirukāmākṣaṇa Perumāl. The temple name derives from "Tirukāmā" (beloved Lord) and "aṣa" (to praise). The annual Brahmotsavam and the Aṣṭa-dala-pūjā are celebrated. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is known for its ancient architecture and the annual float festival (Theppam). ---

title: Tirukkalga Divya Deśam
description: The Tirukkalga Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Kalga Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the battle (yuddha) and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tirukkannapura Divya Deśam
description: The Tirukkannapura Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Kannapura Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the town of Kannapura and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tirukkōḷūr Temple
description: The Tirukkōḷūr Temple (Tamil Nadu), one of the 108 Divya Deśams, the birthplace of Naṭhāmuṉi (the first Āḻvār of the post-Sangam era), dedicated to Viṣṇu as Vaiṭhamanīdhi.

title: Tirukolla-paḍi Divya Deśam
description: The Tirukolla-paḍi Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Kollam-Paḍi Perumāl (the Lord of the collection/harvest). The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the sage Agastya and the Kollam era. ---

title: Tirukkoṣṭiyūr Divya Deśam
description: The Tirukkoṣṭiyūr Temple (Sowrīrāja Perumāl) in Sivaganga district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam where Viṣṇu taught the Tirumantra (Oṃ Namo Nārāyaṇāya) to Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The deity is Sowrīrāja Perumāl with Śrīdevi and Bhūdevi. The temple is the birthplace of Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār's guru (Nampiḷḷai). Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār and Nammāḻvār. The annual Tirumantra-upadeśa festival commemorates the teaching. ---

title: Tirukkoṭṭaṇam Divya Deśam
description: The Tirukkoṭṭaṇam Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Koṭṭaṇam Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the fort (koṭṭam) and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tirukovilur Divya Deśam
description: The Kāmeshvara Temple at Tirukkovilur (Tiruvannamalai district, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Aparājiteśvara/Kāmeśvara. The Pallava-Chola temple with a 7th-century origin. The annual Maha Śivarātri and the Brahmotsavam are major festivals. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The nearby Tiruvōndrēśvara (Tiruvannamalai) temple of Śiva is part of the same complex. ---

title: Tirukkurunkudi Divya Deśam
description: The Nambi Temple at Tirukkurunkudi (Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Nambi (the Lord) in a standing posture with Śrīdevi and Bhūdevi. At the foot of the Western Ghats (Mahendragiri Hills). The Cōḷa-period temple with a beautiful vimāna and the Tirupparkadal (milk ocean) tank. Glorified by Nammāḻvār (who was born nearby) and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Nammāḻvār-avatāra-utsavam are major festivals. One of the southernmost Divya Deśams. ---

title: Tirukuttaḷapādi Divya Deśam
description: The Tirukuttaḷapādi Temple at Kutralam (Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Kutralan/Kūṭṭalai Perumāl. Located on the banks of the Tambraparni River near the famous Kutralam waterfalls. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Kudamuzhala festival are celebrated. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the sage Agastya and the Kutralam region (the "land of the bow" from Sanskrit kodaṁ-lam). ---

title: Tirumalāgiri Divya Deśam
description: The Tirumalāgiri Temple in Karimnagar district (Telangana/Andhra Pradesh), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tirumalāgiri Perumāl. Located on a hilltop with panoramic views. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Maṅgapraśana festival are celebrated. Glorified by Tiruppaṇ Āḻvār and Tirumāldevar. The temple is associated with the story of the sage Gautama and the divine tank (Pushkarinī). ---

title: Tirumalai Divya Deśam
description: The Tirumalai Temple (Tirumalai Nambi) near Tirupati (Andhra Pradesh/Tamil Nadu border), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Nambi (the Lord). A hill temple at 600m elevation with 600 steps. The deity is in standing posture with Śrīdevi and Bhūdevi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Tiruppāvai festival are celebrated. One of the lesser-known but historically important Divya Deśams near the Tirupati complex. ---

title: Tirumanikūṇḍa Divya Deśam
description: The Tirumanikūṇḍa Temple at Kanyakumari district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tirumanikūṇḍa Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the precious stone (mani) and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tirumukkūḍal Divya Deśam
description: The Tirumukkūḍal Temple at Kumbakonam (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to the three deities in one: Viṣṇu (Nārāyaṇa), Brahmā, and Rudra (Śiva). The unique trinity (tri-devata) temple representing the Trimūrti in one sanctum. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Maha Shivaratri are celebrated. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār and Nammāḻvār. The temple represents the concept of Trimūrti in one form (Tirumukkūḍal = "three-joined"). ---

title: Tirunāvāya Divya Deśam
description: The Navamukunda Temple at Tirunāvāya (Malappuram, Kerala), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Navamukunda (nine-faced). On the banks of the Bhāratappuzha (Nīlā) river. The annual Karkkaṭaka-vāvu (ancestor rites) draws thousands. The temple is associated with the Māmāṅkam festival (medieval trade fair). Glorified by Nammāḻvār and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The Kerala-style architecture with a round sanctum (vṛtta-śikhara). One of the few Divya Deśams in Kerala. ---

title: Tirupariśrīmala Divya Deśam
description: The Tirupariśrīmala Temple at Tirupati district (Andhra Pradesh), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Pariśrīmala Perumāl (the fully auspicious Lord). The temple is known for its fine sculpture and architecture. The annual Parikrama and the Brahmotsavam are celebrated. Glorified by Tiruppaṇ Āḻvār. The temple tank (Pushkarinī) is associated with the story of the sage Agastya. ---

title: Tiruppaṅkala Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppaṅkala Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Paṅkala Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the bamboo grove (paṅkala) and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tiruppaṇṇiyūr Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppaṇṇiyūr Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Pāṇiyūr Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the sage Pāṇi and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tirupparāṅkuḍi Divya Deśam
description: The Tirupparāṅkuḍi Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Azhimukham (the face of the Lord). Located near the Courtallam waterfalls. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Theppam (float festival) are celebrated. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple tank (Pushkarinī) is associated with the Western Ghats. ---

title: Tirupparāṅkaḷam Divya Deśam
description: The Tirupparāṅkaḷam Temple at Thiruvananthapuram district (Kerala/Tamil Nadu border), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Parāṅkaḷam Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the sage Para and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tirupparāntasar Divya Deśam
description: The Tirupparāntasar Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Parāntasar Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the sage Parāntara and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tirupparavasaram Divya Deśam
description: The Tirupparavasaram Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Paravasara Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the sage Paravasara and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tiruppariyālūr Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppariyālūr Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Pariyālūr Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the sage Pariyāla. ---

title: Tiruppāṟkaṭal Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppāṟkaṭal Temple (the Ocean of Milk) at Kāñcīpuram (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam where Viṣṇu reclines on Ādiśeṣa in the Kṣīrasāgara (ocean of milk). The temple is associated with the Pāṟkaṭal (the milk ocean) where the Devas and Asuras churned for amṛta. Glorified by Poygai Āḻvār, Bhūta Āḻvār, and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The annual Kṣīrābdhi-navamī festival celebrates the churning. A small but theologically important Divya Deśam representing the cosmic ocean. ---

title: Tiruppaṭṭanam Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppaṭṭanam Temple near Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala/Tamil Nadu border), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Thiruppaṭṭanam Perumāl. Located in the ancient port town of Pāṇṭyāṅkal. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Āvaḻpōcchai. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the maritime trade of the ancient Tamil coast. ---

title: Tiruppattinam Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppattinam Temple in Kanyakumari district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Perumāl. Located on the southern tip of the Tamil coast, near the sea. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Navaratri festivals are celebrated. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the sage Agastya and the southern boundary of the ancient Tamil land (Tamilakam). ---

title: Tiruppaṭṭi-puliyūr Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppaṭṭi-puliyūr Temple near Cuddalore (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Paṭṭi-puliyūr Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the tiger (puli) and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tiruppernamal Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppernamal Temple (Thiruppernamal) near Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu, a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tiruppernamal Perumāl. Associated with the story of Pṛthu (the first king to perform yajña) and the giving-up of the kingdom. The annual Aṅga-dwādashi festival is celebrated. Glorified by Nammāḻvār and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is also associated with the sage Durvāsa and the Swayambhū (self-manifested) deity. ---

title: Tiruppugal-ūr Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppugalūr Temple at Tiruppugalūr (Tiruvarur district, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tiruppugalūr Perumāl. Located near the historical battlefield of Kalinga-pattinam. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aṅgaḻirai. Glorified by Tirumazhisai Āḻvār and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple has a beautiful gopuram and a large temple tank. ---

title: Tiruppuliyūr Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppuliyūr Temple at Cuddalore district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tiruppuliyūr Perumāl. Located near the Pulicat Lake. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the story of the tiger (puli) and the devotee. ---

title: Tiruppulla-bhūta Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruppulla-bhūta Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Pulla-bhūta Perumāl. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the grass (pulla) and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tiruppullāṇi Divya Deśam
description: The Ādi Jagannātha Temple at Tiruppullāṇi (near Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Ādi Jagannātha (the original Jagannātha) in a reclining posture. The legend: Rāma performed śrāddha for his father Daśaratha here; the temple marks the spot where Rāma prayed to Viṣṇu before crossing to Lanka. The sacred tīrtha (Darbha-śayana-tīrtha) is famous. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār and Nammāḻvār. The annual Rāma-navamī and the Ādi-amāvāsyā festivals are celebrated. ---

title: Tiruvāṭi Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruvāṭi Temple at Tiruvāṭi (near Thiruvalla, Kerala), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tiruvāṭi Perumāl. The temple is associated with the sage Durvāsa and the river Maṇimala. The annual festival coincides with the Makara-saṅkrāmaṇa. Glorified by Nammāḻvār. The Kerala-style architecture with a nalukettu layout. One of the Divya Deśams in the Travancore region. ---

title: Tiruvallikēṇi Divya Deśam
description: The Pārthasārathi Temple at Tiruvallikēṇi (Triplicane, Chennai, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Pārthasārathi (Kṛṣṇa as Arjuna's charioteer). The 8th-century Pallava temple, expanded by the Cōḷas and Vijayanagara. Five sancta: Pārthasārathi, Ranganātha, Rāma, Narasiṃha, and Varāha. The temple tank (Kairavinī) is famous for the float festival (Teppa-utsavam). Glorified by Poygai Āḻvār, Bhūta Āḻvār, Pēy Āḻvār, Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār, and Nammāḻvār. One of the oldest Divya Deśams in an urban setting. ---

title: Tiruvānana-pura Divya Deśam
description: The Anantasayana Temple at Tiruvānana-pura (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Anantasayana (reclining on the cosmic serpent). The deity is in reclining posture on Ādiśeṣa, with the hill temple offering a panoramic view. The annual Anavasyava Ekādaśī and the annual temple car festival are celebrated. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple gives its name to the city of Thiruvananthapuram. ---

title: Tiruvaramudreśvara Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruvaramudreśvara Temple at Tiruvanmiyur (Chennai, Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tiruvaramudreśvara (the Lord of the fragrant place). A 7th-century Pallava temple with beautiful early Chola bronzes. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Aṅga-pūrṇa festival are celebrated. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple tank (Pushkarinī) is associated with the legend of the sage Agastya. The nearby Parthasarathy Temple (Triplicane) is another Divya Deśam. ---

title: Tiruvāṇṇamalai Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruvāṇṇamalai Temple at Tiruvāṇṇamalai (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Arunachalesvara (the Lord of the red hill). The temple is associated with the sacred hill (Arunachala) worshipped by Śaṅkara and Ramana Maharshi. The annual Brahmotsavam and the Mahashivaratri are celebrated. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is also a major Śaiva pilgrimage site. ---

title: Tiruvānthamālai Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruvānthamālai Temple at Tirunelveli district (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Vānthamālai Perumāl (the Lord with garlands of flowers). The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is associated with the legend of the flower garlands and the divine intervention. ---

title: Tiruvarāha Koṭṭa Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruvarāha Koṭṭa Temple at Tirupati district (Andhra Pradesh), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Vārāha (boar avatāra). Located near the Tirumala hills. The temple is associated with the rescue of Bhūmi-devī (the Earth goddess) by Vārāha. The annual Vāsudeva Ekādaśī is the main festival. Glorified by Tiruppaṇ Āḻvār, Periyāḻvār, and Tirumāldevar. The nearby cave of Bāṇa is associated with the story. The sanctum houses a 12-foot Vārāha deity. ---

title: Tiruvarasagara Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruvarasagara Temple at Guntur district (Andhra Pradesh), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Varasagara Perumāl. The temple is associated with the legend of the sage Agastya and the divine tank. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tiruppaṇ Āḻvār. The temple architecture follows the local style with a modest gopuram. ---

title: Tiruvāy-mara Divya Deśam
description: The Tiruvāy-mara Temple near Chennai (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tiruvāy-mara Perumāl (the Lord under the banyan tree). Associated with the banyan tree (vāy-tree) where Viṣṇu rested. The annual festival coincides with the Tamil month of Āvaḻpōcchai (mid-Feb). Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is in a rural setting near Tambaram. ---

title: Tiru-Vellāṅkaṇṇi Divya Deśam
description: The Tiru-Vellāṅkaṇṇi Temple (Vellankanni) at Tiru-Vellāṅkaṇṇi (Tamil Nadu), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Tiru-Vellāṅkaṇṇi Perumāl. The temple is associated with the legend of the sage Agastya and the goddess. The annual festival is celebrated during the Tamil month of Aippāsi. Glorified by Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple is also known as the "Rome of India" for the basilica church built later by Portuguese missionaries. ---

title: Tṛkkākkāra Divya Deśam
description: The Tṛkkākkāra Temple (Vāmana Mūrti) at Tṛkkākkāra near Kochi (Kerala), a Divya Deśam dedicated to Viṣṇu as Vāmana (the dwarf avatāra). The only Divya Deśam in Kerala proper. The legend: Vāmana placed his third step on Mahābali's head here. The annual Onam festival (ten days) celebrates Mahābali's visit, culminating in the Vāmana-jayantī. Glorified by Nammāḻvār and Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār. The temple follows the Kerala architectural style with a copper-plated roof. ---

title: Tirumala Tirupati Divya Deśam
description: The Veṅkaṭeśvara Temple at Tirumala (Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh), a Divya Deśam and the most visited pilgrimage site in India (30-40 million annually). Dedicated to Viṣṇu as Veṅkaṭeśvara (Lord of Veṅkaṭa Hill). The Dravidian architecture with gold-plated vimāna (Ananda Nilayam). Glorified by Nammāḻvār, Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār, Kulasekhara Āḻvār, and Tiruppaṇ Āḻvār. The Tirumalā-Tirupati Devasthānams (TTD) manages the temple. The Brahmotsavam (9-day festival) and the weekly Śeṣa-vāhana-sevā are major events. The laddū-prasādam is world-famous. ---

title: Tryambakeśvara Temple Nashik
description: The Tryambakeśvara Temple at Nashik (Maharashtra), one of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas, situated near the source of the Godāvarī river, with the unique three-faced liṅga representing Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.

title: Vaishno Devi Temple
description: The Vaishno Devi Temple in the Trikuta Mountains (Jammu & Kashmir), one of the fifty-one Śakti Pīṭhas, where the right hand of Devī fell, a major pilgrimage site dedicated to Devī as Vaishno Devi/Mahākālī/Mahālakṣmī/Mahāsarasvatī.

title: Darśana
description: A classification for philosophical systems represented as distinct schools rather than one homogeneous position.

title: Deity traditions
description: A classification for deity-centered textual and living traditions without imposing theological hierarchy.

title: Festival traditions
description: A classification for festivals and observances whose forms vary by region, community and tradition.

title: Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava tradition
description: Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava tradition is the Kr̥ṣṇa-bhakti sampradāya initiated by Caitanya Mahāprabhu (1486–1533) in 16th-century Bengal, who taught the 'yuga-dharma' of congregational chanting of the holy names (kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana) as the prime practice of the age. Its theology centers the dovetailing of the individual soul (jīva) with Kr̥ṣṇa's eternal rasa-līlā (the 'rasa of the gopīs'), expressed through the progressive stages of devotion (sādhana-bhakti → prema, divine love), and is codified in the writings of the Six Gosvāmīs (Rūpa, Sanātana, Jīva, Gopala Bhaṭṭa, Dhāmodara, and Raghunātha dasa). Its centers include the holy dham (sacred geography) of Nabadwip (the birthplace of Caitanya) and Vṛndāvana (the childhood place of Kr̥ṣṇa), and it should not be conflated with the other Vaiṣṇava traditions of India (e.g., the Vallabha school of Rajasthan and the Vaiṣṇava schools of South India).

title: Liṅgāyat tradition
description: Lingayata is the medieval Karnataka tradition of the Liṅga-śiva, reformed and systematized in the 12th century by Basavānī (Basavānī, 1106–1167), Allama Prabhu, and the Veeragāṇa saints. Its hallmarks are the daily worship of the liṅga (the 'universal symbol of Śiva' as the 'body of Śiva') worn always, the egalitarian rejection of caste, the Veera-saṅgīṇa (military-saint) poetry composed in the language of the saints, and the ethics of 'work as worship' (kāyaka). Its distinct institutions include the Piḷḷaṇa mathas and the Śākti-pīṭha (the temple of the Liṅga) of Karnataka, and it should not be conflated with the Śaiva Siddhānta or the other Śaiva traditions of South India.

title: Practice
description: A portal classification for lived practices, not a claim that all communities practice in the same way.

title: Sanskrit
description: A language and literary domain represented here through texts, terms, grammar and transmission rather than as a single uniform tradition.

title: Śaiva traditions
description: A broad category for Śiva-centered traditions with diverse textual, ritual, and regional forms; not presented as a single organization.

title: Śākta traditions
description: A broad category for Devī-centered traditions with diverse textual, ritual, and regional forms; not presented as a single organization.

title: Smārta traditions
description: A tradition associated with the worship of five deities (pañcāyatana) and the Advaita Vedānta framework; its boundaries and practices vary regionally.

title: Śrī Vaiṣṇava tradition
description: A Vaiṣṇava tradition associated with Rāmānuja and the Viśiṣṭādvaita framework; its temple and monastic institutions are distinct from other Vaiṣṇava lineages.

title: Upaniṣads
description: A broad category for Upaniṣadic texts, represented with attention to differences among texts, recensions and interpretations.

title: Vaiṣṇava traditions
description: A broad category for traditions centered on Viṣṇu or related forms; it contains diverse lineages and should not be treated as one organization.

title: Vedāṅga
description: A classification for auxiliary disciplines associated with Vedic study; its individual domains have distinct histories and textual materials.
